MoChat's free-form chat replies and some everyday messages are generated during play by AI. By default, a local language model runs on the player's PC, and chat content is not sent to external servers for AI generation.
Optionally, Windows players can connect their own API key from OpenAI, Anthropic (Claude), Google (Gemini) or xAI (Grok) in Settings instead. Only while this option is on, the player's chat messages, recent chat history, saved chat memories and the character's profile are sent directly from the player's PC to the selected provider to generate replies, under that provider's terms (for example, Google may use chats sent through Gemini's free tier to improve its products), and usage is billed to the player's own account. The key is encrypted by Windows and stored only on the player's PC. It is never sent to WhyDuck Studio. Players can delete the key or switch back to the local model at any time.
Characters are designed to follow developer-written personalities and content safety rules intended for all-ages conversations, whichever model is used. AI generates chat text only. Generative AI was also used to create some visual assets. These assets are not generated live during play.

We're a team passionate about pushing the boundaries of game development. This game is where human creativity meets cutting-edge technology. We use AI as a powerful co-pilot for our artists and designers to bring their vision to life never as a replacement.
Our Philosophy: Human-Led Innovation
A Tool for Artists: This isn't a game made by AI. It's a game made by our team of artists and designers using a new generation of smart tools to build a world we couldn't have even dreamed of a few years ago. All of our 3D game props are hand-crafted. Every key asset, every character, and every story beat starts and ends in the hands of our real hands.
An Ethical & Transparent Approach: We are committed to the ethical use of this technology. That means our AI is guided by human creativity at every step and trained on our own original and ethically-sourced assets, and constantly audited to ensure a fair experience. The privacy and security of your player data is our highest priority.
What This Means For You: A Deeper, More Dynamic World
By using AI responsibly, we're able to create experiences that just weren't possible with traditional methods:
We create unique experiences:
Store Presence & Character Images: The visuals on our store page were rapidly iterated on with AI tools to find the most compelling composition, all guided by our art director's vision. We used in-game menus leverage AI to generate dynamic, personalized characters backgrounds that reflect your unique journey and achievements in the game.
Music & Soundscapes: Our score is basically advised by real human artists. We use AI as a collaborative partner to generate adaptive layers of music that react to your playstyle in real-time, creating a soundtrack that is truly feels like you in authenticity desert parties to yacht raven music.
Living Characters: Every main character has been designed and hand written by our team. We use AI-powered machine learning systems to add richness and variety to the ambient population, making the world feel more realistic and alive without taking focus away from our handcrafted narrative using cutting-edge technology.
The result? A world that feels more alive, characters with more dynamic stories, and an experience that is uniquely yours.
This is the next evolution in gaming and we want you to be a part of it.

AI-Generated Content Disclosure
This game uses generative AI in the following ways:
- Pre-generated content: part of the store page artwork (capsule images) and some of the
in-game artwork were created with AI image generation tools during development. Every such
asset was reviewed, edited and finalized by the developer before release.
- Live-generated content: NPC dialogue and ambient chatter are generated in real time by an
open-source language model (Qwen2.5) bundled with the game. It runs entirely offline on the
player's own machine via llama.cpp - no external server, no third-party API, and no internet
connection are required. Players can toggle this feature on or off. The model runs locally
using the player's CPU - no data is sent anywhere.

EQUILIBRIUM uses generative AI to power its core gameplay mechanic: the Policy Terminal.
LIVE-GENERATED CONTENT
When a player types a directive or law in natural language (e.g., "Abolish the luxury car tax"), the AI Engine analyzes the request in real time and generates a structured governmental dossier, including:
- Legislative feasibility analysis
- Budget impact and financial coverage
- Macroeconomic effects (GDP, debt, inflation)
- Social and political consensus projections
- Parliamentary vote simulation
Model used: Anthropic Claude, accessed via API.
Guardrails: AI output is constrained to a fixed set of structured fields defined by the developer. All numeric effects are clamped within bounds enforced by the simulation engine, so no AI output can produce values outside the game's defined ranges. The model operates only on the simulation state provided to it and cannot invent game data: commands that cannot be mapped to a valid government action are refused, and the player is offered bounded policy alternatives instead. No image, audio, or user-data generation is involved, and no player data is used to train any model.
Because responses are generated at runtime, outputs vary between playthroughs: the same directive may produce different wording and different outcomes.
PRE-GENERATED CONTENT
The game's background music track was generated using AI tools during development and ships with the game.

We're just a small team who loves making games and we love using AI to make them even better.
We know there’s been a lot of negativity around AI in games lately, and honestly, we get it. But for us, AI isn’t some big scary thing, it’s a tool we use every day with excitement and care. It helps us bring our world to life, and gives players new ways to express their own creativity.
In our game, AI is used to make things feel more alive. It helps players voice their characters, translate their stories for others to enjoy around the world, and build cool things they might not have been able to otherwise. We're not using AI to replace artists or writers, we're using it to give more people the power to create.
We believe in giving players tools, not walls. AI is one of those tools, and we're constantly working to use it in thoughtful, respectful ways that fit our vision and our values.
So if you're on the fence about AI in games, we just ask: give it a chance. We’re doing our best to make something special here. This game is built with love, and we hope that shows in every part of it, even the parts powered by AI.

Sketch Play includes an in-game assistant called Scholia. When you ask her to look at a page, she reads your drawing and writes back her impressions, a few things to try next, and an experience-point reward. That written feedback is generated by Gemma 4 E2B, a small open-weights AI model.
Scholia cannot draw. She has no ability to generate images, alter your artwork, or add anything to the page. Everything in your sketchbook is drawn by you and the people you invite.
The model runs entirely on your own computer. No account or internet connection is required, nothing you draw is uploaded, and none of your work is used to train anything.
